Why one simple word in a recipe can ruin the dish.

Kevin explains how Julia Child, the French chef, tested her cookbook by handing recipes to people and watching them cook. Her recipe said to saute mushrooms, and they threw them whole into a pan and steamed them. She reworded it to brown the mushrooms, and they still steamed them.

Only when she gave very specific instructions, down to slicing button mushrooms about one centimeter thin, did people get it right.

The lesson: the small details of a method matter as much as the method itself.

Where have you skipped a small detail and missed the result?
